mechanism_narrative: The sustained decline in RETAIL_REC over the last four weeks, culminating in the lowest point at t-0w, indicates a persistent downward trend that will continue to depress retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed trend.

mechanism_narrative: The significant increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility to its highest point at t-0w (10.0%) indicates a strong public preference for staying home, which directly reduces out-of-home activities like retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 5% in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC shows a significant increase.

mechanism_narrative: The combined sharp decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility at t-0w, alongside the rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility, suggests a tightening of official or unofficial restrictions that will suppress retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility both rise by more than 5 percentage points in the next two weeks, while RETAIL_REC remains low.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of declining outdoor activity, the sharp drop in PARKS mobility at t-0w to its lowest point (-31.1%) signals a broader reduction in discretionary outdoor movement, which will also impact retail and recreation negatively over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rebounds by more than 10 percentage points in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC increases.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in RETAIL_REC of more than 5 percentage points, as observed from t-1w to t-0w (-30.1% to -35.6%), indicates accelerating avoidance behavior that will continue to depress retail and recreation in the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC drops by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the next week despite a previous week-on-week drop of more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and significant decline in WORKPLACES mobility, reaching -26.3% at t-0w, reflects ongoing or intensifying work-from-home mandates or advisories, which reduces foot traffic to retail and recreation establishments over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility shows a sustained increase for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility is negative (indicating reduced essential trips) AND RESIDENTIAL mobility is high (indicating increased time at home), it signals a broad reduction in all types of out-of-home activity, including retail and recreation, over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains negative and RESIDENTIAL remains high, but RETAIL_REC increases significantly over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a context where all non-residential mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) are significantly below baseline, the current state represents a deep suppression of activity that will persist over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: At least two non-residential proxies rebound above -5% in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC shows an increase.
